author: Temminck, 1831
summary: 작은 무리를 지어 드물게 한반도를 지나가는 나그네새이다. 산지 낙엽활엽수림에 살며, 곤충을 주로 먹지만 지네, 지렁이와 장미과·포도과 열매도 먹는다. 잡목림, 낙엽활엽수림, 관목 숲에 둥지를 짓고 5월 초순~7월 하순에 알을 3~4개 낳는다. 일본과 중국 중부에서 번식하고, 일본 서남부, 중국 동부와 남부, 인도차이나반도 등지에서 겨울을 난다.

sexes.male: 머리부터 꼬리까지 윗면과 멱, 가슴이 검고, 흰 배에 불규칙한 검은 반점이 있다.

art.subject: Japanese Thrush (Turdus cardis), adult male on spring passage: head, neck, throat, breast and the whole upperparts including wings and tail deep slate-black; a clean border between the black breast and the white lower breast and belly, which carry bold, irregular black spots, densest on the breast sides and flanks; undertail coverts white; bill bright yellow; a narrow yellow eye-ring around the dark eye; pale yellow legs.
art.pose: perched on a branch in deciduous woodland, side view
art.scene: Korean mountain deciduous broadleaf forest on passage; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, side view perched on a branch: slate-black head, breast and upperparts, white belly with bold irregular black spots on the breast sides and flanks, yellow bill, narrow yellow eye-ring, yellow legs

adult female, side view perched: olive-brown upperparts, whitish throat with dark malar streaks, white underparts with dark brown spots on the breast and flanks, orange-buff wash on the breast sides and flanks, yellowish bill, pale yellowish legs
art.build: Medium-small thrush, 21.5cm, clearly larger than a sparrow and smaller than a pigeon, slimmer and smaller than Pale Thrush (Turdus pallidus). Typical Turdus shape: rounded head, straight bill about two-thirds of the head length, fairly long legs, medium-length square tail. Perches upright on branches and hops on the forest floor with the tail level.
avoid: Do not paint a white supercilium — that belongs to Siberian Thrush (Geokichla sibirica); the male Japanese Thrush has a plain black head.
Do not make the belly all black or unspotted; the black ends at the breast and the white belly carries bold black spots.
Do not give the male orange flanks or a grey back — that is Grey-backed Thrush (Turdus hortulorum).
Do not paint a dark bill; it is yellow in both sexes.
